- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior high), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative sentiment values), model underreacts to downward trend; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model may lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.3+), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day toward historical mean.
